title: yq: alias sync, anchor marks and the alias redirect apply only to the last document of a multi-document stream
body:
**Severity: Medium** — silent wrong values and dropped anchors in every document but the last of a stream.

## Summary

In a multi-document YAML stream, alias value sync (#711), anchor/alias mark preservation (#763) and the #1351 alias redirect apply only to the **last** document. Every earlier document is written positionally with its `&x`/`*x` marks dropped. Found by the review of PR #2510; reproduces on `main` (`a353c85ba`) before that PR, so it is pre-existing.

## Repro

Verified against Homebrew `yq` v4.53.3:

```console
$ printf 'a: &x {p: 1}\nb: *x\n---\na: &x {p: 3}\nb: *x\n' | yq '.b.p = 9'
a: &x {p: 9}
b: *x
---
a: &x {p: 9}
b: *x

$ printf 'a: &x {p: 1}\nb: *x\n---\na: &x {p: 3}\nb: *x\n' | succinctly yq '.a.p = 9'   # main
a: {p: 9}
b:
  p: 1
---
a: &x {p: 9}
b: *x
```

Document 0 loses `&x`/`*x` and `b` does not follow the anchor write; document 1 is right. With three documents only the third is right; `--doc 0` reproduces on its own.

## Root cause (not isolated)

Something in the per-document path of `evaluate_yaml_cursor` — `cursor.index().has_aliases()`, `collect_alias_groups(cursor)`, or the comment-tree capture — answers for the whole stream or for the final document rather than the document at hand. `has_aliases()` being an index-wide flag while `collect_alias_groups` walks the per-document cursor is the first thing to check.

## Suggested fix direction

Make the alias-sensitivity gate and the group collection per document (or per document cursor), then add multi-document twins of the existing `#711`/`#763`/`#1351` CLI tests, including `--doc 0`.

## Why this is separate from #1351

#1351 (PR #2510) changes what a write does inside one document; this is about which documents of a stream get that treatment at all, and it predates the PR.

title: yq: =`'s right side still yields false for a zero-node literal/constructor operand (#2540 residual)
body:
## Summary

[#2540](https://github.com/rust-works/succinctly/issues/2540) fixed `and`/`or`'s own read-only-context handling of a literal/constructor operand whose upstream pipe stage produced zero nodes (e.g. `(.a.zz | true) and true` now correctly answers `true`, matching real yq). The identical `Context.DontAutoCreate` mechanism (#2470) also applies to `=`'s right side, and it diverges the same way:

```console
$ printf 'a:\n  b: 1\nx: 5\n' | yq -o=json -I0 '.x = (.a.zz | true)'
{"a":{"b":1},"x":true}
$ printf 'a:\n  b: 1\nx: 5\n' | succinctly yq -o=json -I0 '.x = (.a.zz | true)'
{"a":{"b":1},"x":5}
```

Real yq gives `x: true`; succinctly leaves `x` unchanged (`5`).

## Why #2540 didn't cover this

`and`/`or` evaluate their operands through `jq::eval::boolean_fanout_bools`, shared by both evaluators, which is where #2540's fix (`yq_empty_context_literal_or_constructor`) was added. `=`'s right side evaluates through a completely separate mechanism (`jq::eval::yq_prepare_assign_targets`/`resolve_dynamic_indexes`), which #2540 did not touch — fixing this needs its own trace through that code path, not a second call to the same classifier from the wrong place.

## Suggested approach

Find wherever `=`'s right side currently registers "zero outputs" for the empty-context case (likely near `yq_prepare_assign_targets`'s own handling of a read-only right-side evaluation, #2470/#2481) and consult `jq::eval::yq_empty_context_literal_or_constructor` there the same way `boolean_fanout_bools` now does, before falling through to the existing "target unchanged" behavior.

## Verification notes

Re-verify the same shape matrix #2540 already established (literal, `[...]` — regardless of body, `{...}` — only when every field value also independently qualifies) against `=`'s right side specifically, since the surrounding mechanism differs even though the underlying "is this operand really empty" classification should be identical.

## Related

- #2540 (fixed `and`/`or`'s own copy of this gap)
- #2470 (the read-only context mechanism both share)
- `docs/compliance/yq/limitations.md`'s "An `and`/`or` operand's evaluation context" section, which already documents this residual

title: yq: a mapping key's anchor is still dropped on the DOM write path (=, |=, del(), -P, --arg)
body:
## Background

#1352 fixed `write_yaml_field_key` (`src/yaml/light.rs`) to emit a mapping
key's own `&anchor`, matching real yq -- but that fix only covers the
cursor-streaming identity path (`YamlCursor::stream_yaml_value`, reached by
a plain `.`/no-op query and `--sort-keys`).

## Remaining bug

The DOM emitter -- reached by a write (`=`, `|=`, `del()`, ...) or a
DOM-forcing flag (`-P`, `--arg`, `-o=json` for JSON output specifically) --
still drops a mapping key's anchor. Confirmed live against yq v4.53.3:

```console
$ printf '&k key: 1\nb: 2\n' | succinctly yq '.b = 5'
key: 1
b: 5
$ printf '&k key: 1\nb: 2\n' | yq '.b = 5'
&k key: 1
b: 5
```

(`-o=json` output is correct in both -- JSON has no anchors to lose.)

## Root cause

`yaml_quote_key` in `src/bin/succinctly/yq_runner.rs` takes only the key
string; nothing in the DOM write path threads a key's anchor mark through
`CommentTree` the way #763 did for *value* anchors (`NodeMeta::anchor` on
`CommentTree::Leaf`/`Array`/`Object`'s own metadata).

## Suggested fix direction

`CommentTree::Object`'s existing key-scoped map (`IndexMap<String, (String,
bool)>`, #765's per-key deferred-value comment slot) is the natural place
for a key anchor mark to join, per #1352's own suggested fix direction --
rather than a fourth parallel structure. This needs threading through:
- the builder (`to_owned_with_comments`/`to_owned_with_comments_at_depth`,
  capturing `field.key_cursor().anchor()` per field)
- `reconcile_presentation_at_depth` (keeping a field's key anchor when the
  write didn't touch that field)
- the DOM emitter (`emit_yaml_value`/`yaml_quote_key` in `yq_runner.rs`)
- likely `enforce_anchor_soundness` too, if a key anchor can itself be an
  alias target elsewhere in the document (unconfirmed -- worth checking
  whether real yq even permits aliasing to a key-anchored node's value this
  way before assuming symmetry with #763's soundness handling).

Larger and riskier than #1352's own scope (which is why it wasn't attempted
there), similar in shape to #763's own original build-out.

title: yq: M2 streaming path still emits a raw (non-escape-sequence) U+2028/U+2029 byte unescaped in JSON output
body:
## Background

#1982 fixed `succinctly yq`'s DOM output path (`-P`, `--arg`, `-r`/`-j`/`-0`,
`--eval-all`, `--split-exp`, and other materializing routes) to escape
U+2028/U+2029 (line/paragraph separator) in JSON output, matching real yq
(confirmed live against v4.53.3: it escapes both unconditionally, regardless
of source).

## Remaining bug

The M2 streaming path (used by a plain identity query, `.`, and most simple
navigation filters) still emits both separators raw when they arrive as an
actual UTF-8 byte already present in the source -- as opposed to a YAML
`\L`/`\P` escape sequence, which the streaming transcoder
(`stream_transcode_double_quoted_to_json` in `src/yaml/light.rs`) already
special-cases correctly.

Confirmed reproducible against real yq v4.53.3, using a JSON input file with
a literal UTF-8 U+2028/U+2029 byte in a string value (not a YAML `\L`/`\P`
escape -- JSON input is a syntactic subset of YAML flow, per #996, so it goes
through the same YAML parser/streaming writer):

```console
$ printf '{"a": "x\xe2\x80\xa8y\xe2\x80\xa9z"}' | succinctly yq -o json -I0 '.'
{"a":"xy z"}          # <- WRONG: raw separator bytes, unescaped
$ printf '{"a": "x\xe2\x80\xa8y\xe2\x80\xa9z"}' | yq -o json -I0 '.'
{"a":"x\u2028y\u2029z"}
```

## Root cause (hypothesis)

Same shape as #2591 (a zero-copy fast path that echoes a source span
verbatim when it contains no backslash-escape, without checking for a
different kind of "needs escaping on output" condition). The streaming
transcoder's own fast path presumably only special-cases the *decoded*
`\L`/`\P` two-character escape sequence as it's being transcoded
character-by-character, but has a separate byte-span-copying fast path for
runs with no backslash at all -- which a raw U+2028/U+2029 byte would take,
since it's not preceded by a backslash in the source. Not yet located
precisely; needs the same kind of investigation #1982's own fix required
(tracing which conversion/transcoding function the plain identity route
actually calls).

## Suggested fix direction

Likely the same shape as #1982's DOM-path fix (`write_json_body_yq`'s new
`write_yq_span_escaping_separators` helper, gated on a cheap `contains(0xE2)`
byte-existence probe before doing a per-character walk) -- but applied to
whichever streaming-transcoder fast path is responsible for copying an
unescaped span of double-quoted-scalar content verbatim.

title: perf(jq): re-measure the walk's remaining double position-resolve now that path/key/parent/getpath are off it (#2168 Stage 2)
body:
**Severity: Low** (perf only; no incorrect output). Carried over from #2168, which is now closed.

## What

#2168's own investigation found the cursor walk resolves each node's `text_position` two
to three times per node: once in `uncons`, again in the delimiter/gap checks, and again
in `c.value()` on recursion. #2578 (direction 1) fixed the *seed* `text_position` gallops
from, which recovered most of the per-lookup cost regardless of how many times a node's
position gets resolved. #2604 (direction 2) removed the walk entirely for `path`, `key`,
`parent` and `getpath` — the shapes #2168 was filed about.

What is left running the walk is `select`, the `sort_by`/`unique_by`/`min_by`/`max_by`
family, and `to_owned_cursor_at_depth` — because for those, the subtree walked *is* the
value tested or materialized, not a bounded navigation (see #2604's rationale in
`docs/compliance/jq/limitations.md`). #2168's closing comment on the merged PR says this
narrower remainder is "worth re-measuring against what is left before anyone commits to
it" — with the seed fix and the four-builtin carve-out both in, the double-resolve may no
longer be worth fixing, or may still be a real cost on `select`/`sort_by`-shaped queries
over large documents. Nobody has re-run the numbers since #2604 landed.

## Why file this now

The note that raised it only exists in a comment on #2168, which is now **closed** — so it
won't surface in an open-issue triage, and the actual next step (re-measure, then decide)
was never captured as its own actionable item.

## Suggested approach

Not prescribing a fix. First step is the re-measurement #2168 asked for: A/B `select(f)`
and `sort_by(f)`-shaped queries (large document, condition/key touching most or all of the
subtree) against the current `main`, now that #2578's seed and #2604's carve-out are both
in, and see whether the double-resolve is still a visible fraction of the remaining cost
before deciding whether a fusion pass is worth it.

## Related

- #2168 — where this was originally raised and where the "worth re-measuring" note lives.
- #2578 — the seed fix that already recovered most of the per-lookup cost this issue is about.
- #2604 — removed the walk entirely for `path`/`key`/`parent`/`getpath`, narrowing this
  issue's remaining scope to `select`/`sort_by` family/`to_owned_cursor_at_depth`.

title: yq: `del()`/writes through a `$var` bound from a navigated position diverge from yq's node semantics
body:
**Severity: Low** (refuse-only — exit 1, no document written)

## Summary

Real yq's variables carry **node identity** (the Go `*yaml.Node`), so a write or `del()`
through a `$var` bound from a navigated position acts on *that node* regardless of where the
pipe currently is — or no-ops. succinctly's shared path resolver raises jq's "Invalid path
expression" instead. Found while planning #2042 (2026-09-08); recorded here because
`substitute_bound_var` is shared by both evaluators, so #2042's jq-mode widening has to be
gated on `EvalTag::Jq` and this needs its own oracle matrix.

## Repro (`main` @ baa26d72e vs yq v4.53.3), input `a: {b: 1}` / `c: {b: 1}`

| filter                            | yq v4.53.3                                        | succinctly yq                                                                   |
|-----------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `(.a as $y \| .a \| $y.b) = 5`    | no-op, document unchanged, exit 0                 | `Error: Invalid path expression near attempt to access element "b" of {"b":1}`, exit 1 |
| `(.a as $y \| .c \| $y.b) = 5`    | no-op, exit 0                                     | same error, exit 1                                                               |
| `del(.a as $y \| .c \| $y)`       | deletes **`.a`** (the bound node); output `c: {b: 1}` | `Error: Invalid path expression with result {"b":1}`, exit 1                  |

Rows that already agree (no-op in both): `(.a as $y | .c | $y) = 5`, `(.a as $y | .a | $y) = 5`,
`(. as $x | .c | $x) = 5`.

```console
$ printf 'a:\n  b: 1\nc:\n  b: 1\n' | yq 'del(.a as $y | .c | $y)'
c:
  b: 1
$ printf 'a:\n  b: 1\nc:\n  b: 1\n' | succinctly yq 'del(.a as $y | .c | $y)'
Error: Invalid path expression with result {"b":1}
```

## Notes

- The `del()` row is not jq's register model at all: yq deletes the node `$y` was bound to,
  and the intervening `.c` is irrelevant. Matching it needs a yq-mode rule on
  `EvalSemantics`, not a wider jq gate (ADR-0018: the mode decides).
- The two `= 5` rows are silent no-ops in yq — whether that is designed or a yq bug, it is
  the reference behaviour (rule 3), and a no-op is not one of the divergence conditions.
- Needs a live matrix first (`=`, `|=`, `+=`, `del`, through `$y`, `$y.b`, `$y[0]`, with the
  bound node at `.`, a sibling, and a descendant), the same discipline #1351 used for
  alias writes.

## Related

- #2042 — jq-mode gate widening; must not reach yq mode.
- #1351 — yq write-through-alias, the closest existing yq node-identity model.

title: jq/yq: the yq JSON-escape fork rests on a one-architecture number and a fn-pointer call
body:
**Severity: Low** (perf / verification; split out of #965 item 12)

## Summary

`src/jq/stream.rs` and `src/yaml/light.rs` each carry their own copy of yq's JSON string
escape loop over the same `find_json_escape` SIMD scan. PR #1638 kept them as a deliberate
fork because the two callers appeared to want opposite inlining: adding `#[inline]` to the
shared `jq::escape::write_json_body_yq` cost jq's `arrays keys_unsorted` **+13.9% on a
7950X**, while `light.rs`'s streaming YAML->JSON path reads ~+1% across the yq corpus
*without* the body inlined. The rationale is recorded in `light.rs`'s `stream_json_string`
doc comment and in `docs/parsing/yaml.md`.

Two gaps in that finding, both verifiable now:

1. **Only the x86_64 number exists.** No ARM figure was ever recorded for the jq side, so
   there is no evidence the two callers need opposite inlining on both platforms
   (CLAUDE.md: memory-bound effects do not port across architectures; name both chips).
2. **The jq caller reaches the escaper through a bare `fn` pointer**, which already blocks
   cross-function inlining at that boundary regardless of any attribute on the callee.
   Verified on current `main`: every `escape` parameter in `src/jq/stream.rs` is declared
   `escape: fn(&mut W, &str) -> core::fmt::Result` (four sites, `:473`, `:505`, `:655`,
   `:694`), and `stream_owned_value_json` passes `write_json_body_yq` as a value through
   `stream_owned_value_json_with`; `stream_lazy_keys_json` calls
   `stream_json_string(out, &key, write_json_body_yq)` the same way. The 14% may be an
   artefact of an inlining change interacting with a fn-pointer call, not evidence that the
   two bodies cannot share one definition.

## Proposed work

- Replace the `fn` pointer parameters in `stream.rs` with a generic closure bound
  (`F: Fn(&mut W, &str) -> core::fmt::Result`) so each call site monomorphizes and LLVM
  can inline the escaper at its discretion.
- Re-run #1638's three-way comparison (fork as-is / shared `write_json_body_yq` without
  attribute / shared with `#[inline]`) with `scripts/ab-cli.py`, interleaved, both modes,
  on **both** pinned machines, against a baseline binary built from the merge-base rather
  than an earlier commit of the same branch.
- Decide from the numbers: if the `arrays keys_unsorted` penalty disappears once the
  indirection is gone, collapse `light.rs`'s copy onto `jq::escape::write_json_body_yq`
  and delete the fork's rationale; if it survives on either chip, record the ARM figure
  next to the x86_64 one and keep the fork with the stronger justification.

Per CLAUDE.md's attribution rule, the fn-pointer removal must be measured **on its own**
first (no other change in the binary), so the 14% can be charged to inlining or to the
indirection and not to both at once.

## Why not just do it in #965

#965 is a Tier 3 tracker mixing design questions with mechanical work; this item has no
design question, only a measurement gate, and both bench machines are reachable today. Do
not put a closing keyword against #965 in the PR body.

title: jq/yaml: fold the two hand-maintained cursor-to-OwnedValue walks onto their generic twins
body:
**Severity: Low** (maintenance; split out of #965 items 3 and 8)

## Summary

Two hand-maintained materializer pairs remain after #907, #1247 and #2636, each a full
recursive document-to-`OwnedValue` walk kept in sync by hand with its generic twin. One
design question, two symptoms.

## A. `lazy.rs::cursor_to_owned` / `cursor_to_owned_at_depth` vs `eval_generic::to_owned_cursor` / `to_owned_cursor_at_depth` (item 8)

`src/jq/lazy.rs` hand-writes a JSON-only tree walk (`cursor_to_owned_at_depth`, ~100
lines on current `main`) even though `JsonCursor` already implements the `DocumentCursor`
trait the generic `to_owned_cursor` (`src/jq/eval_generic.rs`, ~100 lines) is written
against. Every cross-cutting fix has had to land twice: #998's nesting guard was added to
the generic walk first and the `lazy.rs` copy was only found once `-e` raw-overflowed the
stack; #1247's decode-error routing and the undecodable-key wording were applied to both by
hand. This is the JSON-specific instance of the shape below.

## B. `yq_runner.rs::yaml_to_owned_value` vs `eval.rs::yaml_value_to_owned_checked` (item 3)

Both take a `YamlCursor`, do the explicit-tag lookup, the quoted-string short-circuit and
the recursive sequence/mapping walk, and share only the innermost `ResolvedScalar` match
(#907). They have since diverged on purpose in one place: the `yq_runner.rs` copy
materializes through `to_owned_value_for_json_bridge` because its output is headed for the
`to_json_for_reindex` round trip that would otherwise flatten a tag-forced `!!float 2`
(#1176), and the `eval.rs` copy drives `DisplayKeyGuard` by hand because it does not go
through `DocumentFields`/`resolve_display_key` (#1801).

## What is not settled

The earlier review of the `StandardJson` pair found that "near-identical" copies in this
family carry real behavioural differences (NaN-sentinel decoding, malformed-UTF-8 fallback),
so the first step is a **behavioural diff**, not a delegate. For A: enumerate what
`cursor_to_owned_at_depth` does that `to_owned_cursor_at_depth` does not (and vice versa),
with a test per difference, before folding. For B: decide whether the `for_json_bridge`
variant is a parameter of one walk or a reason to keep two. A is the better entry point:
JSON-only, both sides already share the fallible `Result<OwnedValue, EvalError>` shape from
#1247, and success there shows the pattern for B.

Recorded on #965 as "no proposed design yet"; that is still true. Do not put a closing
keyword against #965 in a PR body.

title: yq: a metadata assignment nested under `as` (`.b as $x | .a line_comment = $x`) is refused; real yq applies it
body:
## Summary

A yq metadata assignment (`line_comment =`, `style =`, `anchor =`, #798) is refused with an explicit error whenever it sits anywhere other than a top-level pipe stage. The most common shape that hits this is a variable binding feeding the right-hand side:

```
$ printf 'a: 1\nb: hi\n' | yq '.b as $x | .a line_comment = $x'
a: 1 # hi
b: hi
$ printf 'a: 1\nb: hi\n' | succinctly yq '.b as $x | .a line_comment = $x'
Error: metadata assignment (line_comment/style/anchor = ...) is only supported as a top-level pipe stage
```

Verified against pinned yq v4.53.3 and succinctly at `3a3e88140`. The same refusal covers a write inside a `reduce`/`foreach` body or a `def` body.

## Why it is refused today

`resolve_meta_assign_writes` (`src/bin/succinctly/yq_runner.rs`) runs *before* the real evaluation. It flattens the expression's top-level pipe stages, re-evaluates each earlier stage to reach the document the write sees, then evaluates `path(TARGET)` and the right-hand side against that document via `evaluate_input`. A write nested under `Expr::As` would need `$x` bound when its RHS is evaluated, and `evaluate_input` on the RHS alone has no binding. `count_meta_assigns` compares the total number of `MetaAssign` nodes with the number of top-level stages and reports the mismatch rather than letting the nested write silently no-op (the outcome #798's triage ruled out).

Recorded in `docs/compliance/yq/limitations.md` under "Metadata assignment (`PATH <slot> = value`): what `succinctly yq` refuses or drops".

## Possible directions

- Descend `Expr::As { source, body }` in the pre-pass: evaluate `source` against the current document, then evaluate the body's writes with the binding installed (the evaluator already has a scope mechanism for `as`; the pre-pass would need to enter it, or wrap the RHS as `SOURCE as $x | RHS` and evaluate that).
- Longer term, move the write out of the pre-pass entirely: have `eval_meta_assign` (`src/jq/eval.rs`) record `(path, slot, text)` into a thread-local drained by the runner, the way `alias_identity` threads state through a write. That removes the top-level restriction for every construct at once, but needs the ambient path prefix (the spine-2416 `with_path_base` machinery) to turn a stage-relative target into a document path.

## Notes

- Found while reviewing the #798 PR1 branch; the explicit error was added in that review's fixes.
- `.b as $x | (.a style = "double")` has a CLI test pinning the current refusal (`nested_metadata_assignment_is_refused_explicitly` in `tests/yq_cli_tests.rs`); update it deliberately when this lands.

title: yq: navigating after a write (`.a.b = "y" | .a`) drops every comment, anchor and style the write did not touch
body:
## Summary

When a pipe writes to the document and then *navigates* into it, the result loses every piece of presentation the write did not touch: trailing comments, anchors, quoting style. Real yq keeps them.

```
$ printf 'a:\n  b: x # c\n  d: &z "q"\n' | yq '.a.b = "y" | .a'
b: y # c
d: &z "q"
$ printf 'a:\n  b: x # c\n  d: &z "q"\n' | succinctly yq '.a.b = "y" | .a'
b: y
d: q
```

The same happens after `|=` and after a #798 metadata write, which makes the metadata write itself vanish:

```
$ printf 'a:\n  b: x\n' | yq '.a.b style = "double" | .a'
b: "x"
$ printf 'a:\n  b: x\n' | succinctly yq '.a.b style = "double" | .a'
b: x
```

Verified against pinned yq v4.53.3 and succinctly at `3a3e88140`.

## Mechanism

`evaluate_yaml_cursor` (`src/bin/succinctly/yq_runner.rs`) only builds the pristine `CommentTree` snapshot and reconciles presentation when `is_alias_sensitive_assign(expr)` holds, and that predicate's `is_shape_preserving` half returns `false` for a trailing navigation stage. So the result value is a plain `OwnedValue` with an empty tree: no comment, anchor or style survives, and the #798 write pass never runs at all (it is gated on the same `presentation_sync_ctx`).

This is not specific to #798. It is the same hole for every write form, which is why the review fix for #798 documented it under "Three known gaps this write shares with every other write form" in `docs/compliance/yq/limitations.md` rather than erroring.

## Possible direction

Let `is_shape_preserving` admit a *trailing* static-navigation suffix (`.a`, `.a.b`, `.a[0]`) after a shape-preserving prefix, and have the reconcile step navigate the pristine tree by the same steps so the result's subtree keeps its metadata. `static_nav_steps` already exists for exactly this kind of path. A non-static trailing navigation (`.[]`, `.[(.i)]`) can stay unsupported.

## Notes

- Found while reviewing the #798 PR1 branch.
- Related: #1349 (a multi-result filter carries no `CommentTree` at all), which is the other route that drops all presentation.

title: yq: `style = "literal"/"folded"/"tagged"` are refused and an existing block scalar is re-rendered quoted on any DOM write
body:
## Summary

`style = "literal"`, `style = "folded"` and `style = "tagged"` are in real yq's vocabulary and all three render. succinctly parses them and refuses with an explicit "not yet supported" error, because the DOM emitter has no arm for any of them:

```
$ printf 'a: hello\n' | yq '.a style = "literal"'
a: |-
  hello
$ printf 'a: hello\n' | yq '.a style = "folded"'
a: >-
  hello
$ printf 'a: 1\n' | yq '.a style = "tagged"'
a: !!int 1
$ printf 'a: hello\n' | succinctly yq '.a style = "literal"'
Error: style = "literal" is not yet supported
```

The same emitter gap already shows on any DOM write to a document that *contains* a block scalar, with no metadata assignment involved:

```
$ printf 'a: |\n  x\n  y\n' | yq '.b = 1'
a: |
  x
  y
b: 1
$ printf 'a: |\n  x\n  y\n' | succinctly yq '.b = 1'
a: "x\ny\n"
b: 1
$ printf 'a: >\n  x\n  y\n' | succinctly yq '.b = 1'
a: "x y\n"
```

Verified against pinned yq v4.53.3 and succinctly at `3a3e88140`.

## Mechanism

`NodeMeta.style` (`src/jq/eval_generic.rs`) already carries `"literal"`/`"folded"` read from the cursor, but `yaml_quote_string_with_style` (`src/bin/succinctly/yq_runner.rs`) only has arms for `single`/`double` and falls back to `yaml_quote_string`, and nothing renders a tag from a style at all. `RENDERABLE_STYLES` in the same file is the allow-list the #798 write pass checks before refusing.

## What landing this needs

- Block scalar emission in `emit_yaml_value_at_depth`: `|`/`>` with the right chomping indicator (`|-` for no trailing newline, `|` for one, `|+` for more), an indentation indicator when the first line starts with a space, and the folded form's line-wrapping rules. Real yq's folded output above (`x y` followed by a blank line) is go-yaml's, so pin it from the oracle rather than the spec.
- `tagged`: the `!!int`/`!!str`/`!!bool`/`!!float`/`!!null`/`!!map`/`!!seq` tag for the value's type, and it interacts with #747 (explicit source tags are dropped on the DOM path today).
- Then drop the three names from the refusal in the #798 write pass and remove the entry from `docs/compliance/yq/limitations.md`.

## Notes

- Found while reviewing the #798 PR1 branch.
- Related: #747 (tag preservation), #865 (style preservation).

title: yq: a line_comment on a flow-sequence element re-renders the sequence in block form; real yq keeps `[1, 2, # y` + `]`
body:
## Summary

A `line_comment` written onto an element of a *flow* sequence makes succinctly re-render the whole sequence in block form. Real yq keeps the flow form and emits the comment after a trailing comma inside the brackets:

```
$ printf 'a: [1, 2]\n' | yq '.a[1] line_comment = "y"'
a: [1, 2, # y
]
$ printf 'a: [1, 2]\n' | succinctly yq '.a[1] line_comment = "y"'
a:
  - 1
  - 2 # y
```

Same for `.a[-1]`. Both outputs read back as the same value, so this is a rendering divergence, not data loss. Verified against pinned yq v4.53.3 and succinctly at `3a3e88140`.

## Mechanism

`is_flow_safe` (`src/bin/succinctly/yq_runner.rs`) returns `false` for a flow container whose element carries its own comment, because the flow emitter comma-joins elements on one line and has no position for a per-element comment. The container then falls back to block rendering, exactly as an *existing* element comment already does. The #798 write pass reuses that predicate deliberately so a written comment behaves like a captured one.

Recorded in `docs/compliance/yq/limitations.md` under "Two rendering divergences" in the #798 entry.

## Open question before implementing

go-yaml's output here is peculiar (a comment after the last element's comma, then the closing bracket on its own line). Before matching it, measure a few more shapes against the oracle: a comment on a *middle* element (`.a[0] line_comment = "y"` on `[1, 2]`), a flow mapping value (`.a.b line_comment` on `a: {b: 1, c: 2}`), and a nested flow sequence, since the answer decides whether a general "flow container with commented elements" renderer is needed or just the last-element case.

## Notes

- Found while reviewing the #798 PR1 branch.
- Related: #794 (a flow-collection comment before the closing bracket was dropped on identity output).

title: yq: stages before a metadata assignment are evaluated twice, so a side effect in an assignment RHS (`.a = (.b | debug) | .a line_comment = "y"`) fires twice
body:
## Summary

When a pipe contains a #798 metadata assignment (`line_comment =`, `style =`, `anchor =`), every earlier stage is evaluated twice: once by the write pass that works out which document the metadata write sees, and once by the real evaluation. A side effect inside such a stage therefore fires twice:

```
$ printf 'a: 1\nb: 2\n' | succinctly yq --jq-extensions '.a = (.b | debug) | .a line_comment = "y"'
["DEBUG:",2]
["DEBUG:",2]
a: 2 # y
b: 2
$ printf 'a: 1\nb: 2\n' | succinctly yq --jq-extensions '.a = (.b | debug) | .a = .a'
["DEBUG:",2]
a: 2
b: 2
```

Reproduced on succinctly at `3a3e88140`. Real yq has no `debug` (its lexer rejects it), so this is only reachable through `--jq-extensions`, but the duplicated output is wrong on its own terms: the control case prints once.

## Mechanism

`resolve_meta_assign_writes` (`src/bin/succinctly/yq_runner.rs`) runs before evaluation. To make `.a = 2 | .b line_comment = (.a | tostring)` write `# 2` (as real yq does) it re-evaluates each stage preceding the last metadata write through `evaluate_input_quiet` and carries the first output forward as the document the next stage sees. `is_value_identity_stage` exempts a bare `debug`/`debug(msg)` *stage* precisely so its side effect isn't repeated, but a `debug` (or `stderr`, `input`, `halt_error`, ...) nested inside a stage's right-hand side is still re-run.

## Possible directions

- Detect a side-effecting builtin anywhere inside a stage that precedes a metadata write (a walk with `jq::walk::any_subexpr`, the way `count_meta_assigns` already does) and either refuse explicitly or fall back to resolving against the pristine document for that pipe.
- Or remove the re-evaluation entirely by applying the write *during* evaluation (`eval_meta_assign` recording `(path, slot, text)` into a thread-local the runner drains), which is also the route #2705 needs. That makes each stage run exactly once.

## Notes

- Found while reviewing the #798 PR1 branch; the pipe-sequential resolution that introduces the second evaluation was part of that review's fixes.
- `input`/`inputs` would be worse than a duplicated line (they consume input), but they are not shape-preserving so the write pass never runs for a pipe that contains them at top level; only a nested use inside an assignment RHS could reach this.

title: yq: column reports the value's column, not the anchor's, on an anchored node
body:
**Severity: Low** (a wrong number, but a narrow one)

## Summary

`succinctly yq`'s `column` builtin reports the *value's* column where real yq v4.53.3
reports the **anchor's** — so any node carrying an anchor answers differently.

## Repro (confirmed live against yq v4.53.3)

```console
$ printf 'a: !!str 5\nb: &anc [1,2]\n' > meta.yaml

$ yq            -o=json -I=0 '.b | column' meta.yaml   # 4
$ succinctly yq -o=json -I=0 '.b | column' meta.yaml   # 9

$ yq            -o=json -I=0 '.b | line' meta.yaml     # 2
$ succinctly yq -o=json -I=0 '.b | line' meta.yaml     # 2   <- line agrees
```

`b: &anc [1,2]` — column 4 is where `&anc` starts, column 9 is where `[1,2]` starts. yq
anchors the position at the node's first token including its anchor property; succinctly
skips to the value.

`line` agrees, and `anchor`/`style` agree, so this is specific to `column`.

## Found via

[#2626](https://github.com/rust-works/succinctly/issues/2626), which ungated
`eval_single`'s `Expr::Arithmetic` arm. Before that change `.b | (column + 0)` answered
`0` (the wildcard bridge re-rooted the value at a fresh JSON serialization, stubbing the
whole node-metadata family); afterwards it agrees with succinctly's own bare `column`,
i.e. `9`. So #2626 made this **internally consistent while leaving it divergent**, which
is why it is filed separately rather than pinned there — `test_arithmetic_reads_the_real_document_2626`
deliberately omits `column` from its rows and says so, so that it does not pin the wrong
number.

## Suggested direction

Not investigated. Check where `column` derives its text position for an anchored node and
whether the anchor property's span is available at that point — `anchor` already answers
`"anc"` for the same node, so the mark is reachable. Worth checking the same question for
an explicitly *tagged* node (`a: !!str 5`) at the same time, since a tag is the other
property that can precede a value.

title: yq: {$a} inside object construction should silently produce zero output, matching real yq's COLLECT_OBJECT quirk
body:
## Summary

Follow-up from #2724. That issue fixed jq mode's `{$a}` object-construction
shorthand (and the `{$a: expr}` dynamic-key form). yq mode was deliberately
left untouched there -- it still raises the same pre-existing parse error
it always has ("expected identifier, found '$'") -- because real yq's
actual behavior for this shape is a third, unrelated thing: not an error,
and not jq's `{"a":1}` either.

## What real yq actually does

```console
$ printf 'x: 1\n' | yq '1 as $a | {$a}'
$ echo $?
0
```

Empty stdout, exit 0. `--verbose` shows why: yq's `{...}` object-
construction grammar has **no shorthand concept at all** -- confirmed
separately that even the plain (non-`$`) field shorthand is rejected
outright at the lexer level:

```console
$ printf 'x: 1\n' | yq '{x}'
Error: 1:2: lexer: invalid input text "x}"
```

So `{$a}` isn't sugar in real yq -- it's `$a` (an ordinary `GET_VARIABLE`
op) evaluated as a bare, non-`key: value` entry inside `COLLECT_OBJECT`.
The verbose log shows `COLLECT_OBJECT` degrading on an odd/unpaired input:
`"collectObjectOperation, length of rotated is 0"` -> `"PROCESSING
VARIABLE DONE, got back: 0"` -> `"no matching results, nothing to
print"`. It's an incidental quirk of yq's object-collection operator
handling a non-pair entry, not a deliberate feature.

## Why this is separate from #2724

Reproducing this needs new **evaluator**-level behavior (an object-
construction entry that consumes zero pairs and yields nothing), not a
parser change -- #2724's fix was purely parse-time desugaring. It also
interacts with a pre-existing, already-shipped (and separately
undocumented) succinctly extension: succinctly's yq mode *already* accepts
the plain `{x}` shorthand as sugar for `{x: .x}`, which is itself a
divergence from real yq's lexer-level rejection shown above -- so there
are now two separate open questions about how far yq mode's object-
construction sugar should extend past real yq's much stricter grammar,
not one.

## Suggested next step

1. Decide the target: reproduce real yq's exact "bare non-pair entry
   degrades the whole construction to zero output" behavior (ADR-0018's
   preferred bug-for-bug default), or make a documented, deliberate call to
   keep succinctly's existing shorthand-sugar convenience extension and
   accept the divergence (recording it in
   `docs/compliance/yq/limitations.md`, which currently has no entry for
   object-construction shorthand of any kind despite the plain `{x}` case
   already existing and diverging).
2. Whichever is chosen, also close the parallel gap for the plain `{x}`
   shorthand noted above -- it's the same question, just discovered a level
   up.

title: perf(yq): cursor_key's sibling scan makes per-item key/path reads O(fields) each, quadratic over a wide mapping
body:
## Symptom

Any query that asks `key` (or `path`, or `parent`) once per member of a wide
mapping is quadratic in the number of members. Release build, M5 Max, flat
mappings of `kN: N`:

| query | 20k keys | 40k keys | ratio |
|---|---|---|---|
| `[.[] \| key \| path] \| length` | 64.2 s | 275.9 s | 4.3x for 2x input |
| `[.[] \| select(key == "k5")] \| length` | 31.0 s | 125.8 s | 4.1x for 2x input |
| `[.[] \| key \| line] \| length` | 0.02 s | 0.03 s | linear (the walk route) |

A ratio of ~4 for a doubling is the signature of O(n^2). The third row is the
same document and the same `key`, answered by the path-context *walk*, and it
is linear — so this is not `key` being expensive, it is one route being
quadratic.

## Cause

`cursor_slot` (`src/jq/eval_generic.rs`, `cursor_key`'s worker before #2763
renamed it) answers "where does this cursor sit in its parent" by walking the
parent's members until one matches by `same_node`:

```rust
let mut f = fields.clone();
while let Some((field, rest)) = f.uncons() {
    if field.value_cursor.same_node(c) || field.key_cursor.same_node(c) { ... }
    f = rest;
}
```

That is O(fields) per call, and `cursor_path_and_ancestors` calls it once per
level of the climb. Any route that asks it per item — `eval_builtin`'s cursor
arm and the owned-identity pipe both do — pays O(n) per item over an n-member
mapping. The walk route avoids it entirely by carrying the trail, which is why
the third row above is linear.

This predates #2763 and is unchanged by it: the same table on the merge-base
binary gives the same numbers. #2763 only makes the scan's existence easier to
see, because it added a second `same_node` test to the same loop.

## Likely shape of a fix

The member's position is derivable in O(1) from the tree rather than by
scanning: #2763 added `DocumentCursor::prev_sibling` and both indexed formats
lay a member out as consecutive key/value siblings. What is missing is the
*index* — "which member is this" — which `path`/`key`-on-an-array needs. A rank
over the parent's child positions would answer both in O(1)/O(log n) without a
scan, and the BP structure already carries the machinery.

Worth measuring first whether the array arm (`uncons_cursor` counting up to an
index) or the object arm dominates in practice; the table above is object-only.

## Verification notes

- Gate on output identity, and re-run the three rows above at 20k/40k/80k: the
  fix should turn 4.3x-for-2x into ~2x-for-2x, which is the claim.
- `[.[] | key | line]` (the walk route) must stay exactly where it is — it does
  not touch this scan today and a "fix" that routes it through one would be a
  regression.
- Both architectures: the pinned boxes disagree by more than noise on
  memory-bound effects (see CLAUDE.md's benchmarking discipline).

title: yq: comment set-operators (head_comment=, foot_comment=, comments=, tag=) are unimplemented
body:
Spun out of #798, which is being closed as an umbrella. The *read* side of yq's
comment metadata has landed (#2674 grammar, #2690 storage, #2704/#2718 capture,
#2758 getters). The *write* side is still unimplemented for three of the slots.

## What fails today

On `main` (`54658bca0`), `succinctly yq`:

```
$ printf 'a: 1\n' | succinctly yq '.a head_comment = "hi"'
Error: head_comment = ... is not yet supported
$ printf 'a: 1\n' | succinctly yq '.a foot_comment = "bye"'
Error: foot_comment = ... is not yet supported
$ printf 'a: 1\n' | succinctly yq '.a comments = "x"'
Error: comments = ... is not yet supported
$ printf 'a: 1\n' | succinctly yq '.a tag = "!!str"'
Error: tag = ... is not yet supported
```

The grammar accepts all four — `MetaSlot::{HeadComment, FootComment, Comments, Tag}`
parse fine and reach `eval_meta_assign` in `src/jq/eval.rs`, which raises from a
single explicit arm:

```rust
MetaSlot::Tag | MetaSlot::HeadComment | MetaSlot::FootComment | MetaSlot::Comments => {
    suppress_or_raise(EvalError::new(format!("{} = ... is not yet supported", ...)), optional)
}
```

`line_comment =`, `style =` and `anchor =` already work (#2674).

## What real yq does (pinned v4.53.3)

```
$ printf 'a: 1\nb: 2\n' | yq '.a head_comment = "hi"'
a: 1
# hi
b: 2

$ printf 'a: 1\nb: 2\n' | yq '.a foot_comment = "bye"'
a: 1
# bye

b: 2

$ printf 'a: 1 # old\n' | yq '.a comments = "x"'
a: 1 # x
# x

# x

$ printf 'a: 1\n' | yq '.a tag = "!!str"'
a: "1"
```

Notes from those captures:

- `comments = "x"` sets **head, line and foot together** — three separate
  emissions, not one.
- `foot_comment` emits a **blank line after** the comment; `head_comment` does not.
  (Both yq placements above look surprising relative to the key they were set on —
  reproduce them bug-for-bug per ADR-0018, do not "fix" them into what seems right.)
- `tag = "!!str"` is a **coercion**, not just metadata: the scalar is re-emitted
  quoted. That is a different mechanism from the comment slots and may deserve
  splitting out again if it turns out to be the larger half.
- yq clears a comment with the empty string: `... comments = ""` strips every
  comment in the document (`# h\na: 1 # x\nb: 2\n` → `a: 1\nb: 2\n`).

## Also missing: `...` in yq mode

The `... comments = ""` idiom above is yq's documented way to strip all comments,
and succinctly's yq-mode parser rejects the token outright:

```
$ printf 'a: 1\n' | succinctly yq '... comments = ""'
Error: parse error: parse error at position 2: unexpected character '.'
```

`...` is recursive descent including keys (jq's `..` is values only). Whether it
belongs in this issue or its own is an implementation call — it is listed here
because it is the only way to reach the clear-everything behaviour.

## Why it is blocked

The write side has no storage to write into and no emitter to print it:

1. `NodeMeta.head_foot_comment` is `Option<Box<HeadFootComment>>` and is
   hardcoded `None` at **every** construction site — notably
   `to_owned_with_comments_at_depth` in `src/jq/eval_generic.rs`. The field is
   private with no setter. (It is boxed deliberately: un-boxing it re-breaks
   `reconcile_presentation_panics_past_nesting_depth_limit_1005` by growing
   `reconcile_presentation_at_depth`'s frame past its own depth guard — see the
   #2690 history.)
2. Neither emitter prints head/foot comments at all — that is the round-trip gap
   tracked by #2795. **That issue's DOM half is
   a hard prerequisite**: until `emit_yaml_value_at_depth` can print a head/foot
   comment, a successful write would be invisible.

So the ordering is: round-trip PR B (populate `NodeMeta` + DOM emitter) first,
then this.

## Acceptance

- `.a head_comment = "hi"`, `.a foot_comment = "bye"`, `.a comments = "x"` and
  `... comments = ""` match pinned yq v4.53.3 byte-for-byte.
- `tag = "!!str"` coerces, matching yq.
- Differential fuzz against pinned yq over randomly-placed comments, not a
  hand-picked matrix — the write side is directly observable, so this is available
  here in a way it was not for #2704.
- `docs/compliance/yq/limitations.md`: remove the entries these close; record any
  divergence that survives.
- `omni-dev coverage diff` at 100% before pushing.

title: yq: `==`/`!=` never match a container, and unique/group_by key on scalar text -- succinctly answers structurally
body:
## Symptom

#2785 adopted real yq's *scalar* `==`/`!=` rule (text, with `*`/`?` wildcards on the right
operand -- `eval::yq_scalar_text_eq`). Two neighbouring halves of the same `isEquals`
(`pkg/yqlib/operator_equals.go`, v4.53.3) are still answered jq's way. Captured live,
`-o=json -I0`, on `l: [1]\nm: {x: 1}\na: 1\nb: "1"\n`:

| filter                              | yq       | succinctly   |
|-------------------------------------|----------|--------------|
| `[1] == [1]`                        | `false`  | `true`       |
| `.l == .l`, `. == .`                | `false`  | `true`       |
| `{} == {}`, `.m == {"x": 1}`        | `false`  | `true`       |
| `[1] != [1]`                        | `true`   | `false`      |
| `[.a, .b] \| unique`                | `[1]`    | `[1, "1"]`   |
| `[1, "1", 01] \| unique`            | `[1, 1]` | `[1, "1"]`   |
| `[.a, .b] \| group_by(.) \| length` | `1`      | `2`          |
| `[.b, .a] \| sort`                  | `["1", 1]` | `[1, "1"]` |

Real yq's `isEquals` answers `false` unless the left operand is `!!null` (then: right is
`!!null`) or both operands are scalar nodes -- an array or object pairing is never equal,
`. == .` included. `unique`/`unique_by`/`group_by` key their ordered map on the node's
`.Value` text (`getUniqueKeyValue`, `processIntoGroups`), so `1` and `"1"` dedup together
there -- *without* the wildcard, which is why #2785 kept the text rule out of
`owned_value_eq` (#950's shared dedup definition): a glob is neither symmetric nor
transitive and cannot key a map. `sort`'s comparator (`operator_sort.go`) is typed for
null/bool/number pairs and falls back to `strings.Compare` on the text for anything else,
which is how `"1"` sorts before `1` (equal text, stable order).

## Where the code is

- `eval::yq_scalar_text_eq` (`src/jq/eval.rs`) returns `None` for any container operand so
  the structural rule decides; the container half is a one-line change there once the
  fidelity call is made (ADR-0018: nothing here is a rule-4 exception, but `[1] == [1]`
  being `false` is a large behavioural change for `select`-heavy scripts).
- `value::owned_value_eq` is what `unique`/`unique_by`/`group_by`/`contains`/array `-`
  consume; the dedup half wants a text-key beside it, not a change to it.
- Pinned as today's answers by `yq_text_equality_2785::the_rest_of_the_equality_family_is_unchanged_2785`
  (`tests/yq_cli_tests.rs`) and recorded in `docs/compliance/yq/limitations.md`.

Split out of #2785, which needed only the scalar rule to unblock typed key nodes.

title: yq: wildcard (`.["a*"]`, `.a*`) and integer (`.[1]`, `has(1)`) mapping-key traversal are not implemented
body:
## Symptom

Real yq routes every mapping-key lookup through `matchKey` (`pkg/yqlib/matchKeyString.go`,
v4.53.3) -- a byte-level glob where `*` is zero or more bytes and `?` exactly one -- and
matches a key by its *text*, so an integer index also finds an `!!int` key. Captured live,
`-o=json -I0`, on `abc: 1\nabd: 2\nx: 3\n1: y\n`:

| filter                      | yq                                    | succinctly                              |
|-----------------------------|---------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------|
| `.["ab*"]`                  | `1` `2`                               | `null`                                  |
| `.ab*`                      | `1` `2`                               | parse error                             |
| `[.["a?c"]]`                | `[1]`                                 | `[null]`                                |
| `[.["*"]] \| length`        | `4`                                   | `1`                                     |
| `.ab* = 9`                  | `{"abc":9,"abd":9,...}`               | parse error                             |
| `del(.["ab*"])`             | `{"x":3,"1":"y"}`                     | unchanged                               |
| `.[1]`                      | `"y"`                                 | `null`                                  |
| `has(1)`                    | `true`                                | `false`                                 |
| `.[1] = "z"`                | `{...,"1":"z"}`                       | `Cannot index object with number`       |
| `has("ab*")`                | `false`                               | `false` (`has` is exact -- agrees)      |
| `.[] \| select(key == "ab*")` | `1` `2`                             | `1` `2` (#2785's `==` already matches)  |

Two quirks worth capturing before implementing, both live on v4.53.3: `del(.["1"])` and
`del(.[1])` on the `1: y` member are **no-ops** (`.["1"]` reads it fine), and `.["x*y"]`
on no match is `null`, not empty.

## Where the code is

- The matcher already exists: `glob::yq_match_key` (`src/jq/glob.rs`, #2785) is the
  byte-for-byte port used by `==`; traversal needs the same function at the key-lookup
  sites (`find_cursor`/`DocumentFields::get` and the `.[n]`-on-object arm), plus a parser
  change for the bare `.ab*` spelling.
- Recorded in `docs/compliance/yq/limitations.md` under #2785's residuals.

Split out of #2785.

title: yq: `path`/`paths` emit an `!!int` mapping key as an integer component, succinctly always a string
body:
## Symptom

Real yq's path register types an `!!int` mapping key as an integer and every other key
as a string -- `GetPath` renders the key node's text as an int iff its tag is `!!int`.
Captured live, `-o=json -I0`, on `1: x\ntrue: y\nnull: z\n1.5: w\n"2": v\n~: u\n`:

| filter                           | yq                                                    | succinctly                                     |
|----------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------|
| `[.[] \| path]`                  | `[[1],["true"],["null"],["1.5"],["2"],["~"]]`         | `[["1"],["true"],["null"],["1.5"],["2"],["~"]]` |
| `.[] \| select(key == 1) \| path` | `[1]`                                                | `["1"]`                                        |

Only the `!!int` case differs; `true`, `null`, `1.5` and `~` are strings in yq's path too.

## Where the code is

`cursor_slot`/`cursor_key` (`src/jq/eval_generic.rs`) put `OwnedValue::String(display)`
in the path register for every member, and `collect_paths_generic` does the same for
`paths`. Retyping an int-spelled key there needs care: the register's `String`-vs-`Int`
distinction is what `getpath`/`setpath`/`del` use to tell an object key from an array
index, so an `Int` component on an object would have to be accepted by every consumer
before `path` can emit one.

Split out of #2785 (which made the key *node* typed but left the register alone) and
recorded in `docs/compliance/yq/limitations.md`.

title: yq: null/bool/non-canonical-int spellings (`~`, `True`, `01`, `0x1f`, `1_000`) are lost in OwnedValue -- tostring, ==, and from_entries diverge
body:
## Symptom

`OwnedValue::Null`/`Bool`/`Int` carry no source spelling, and `NumberLiteral` is only
kept for JSON-shaped numbers, so any scalar that real yq keeps as its original text
collapses to a canonical rendering once materialized. Captured live, `-o=json -I0`:

| document       | filter               | yq        | succinctly |
|----------------|----------------------|-----------|------------|
| `a: ~`         | `.a \| tostring`     | `"~"`     | `"null"`   |
| `b: True`      | `.b \| tostring`     | `"True"`  | `"true"`   |
| `d: 0x1f`      | `.d \| tostring`     | `"0x1f"`  | `"31"`     |
| `e: 1_000`     | `.e`, `.e \| tag`    | `1000`, `!!int` | `"1_000"`, `!!str` |
| `k: 01`        | `.k \| tostring`     | `"01"`    | `"1"`      |
| `k: 01`        | `.k == "01"`, `.k == 1` | `true`, `false` | `false`, `true` |
| `b: True`      | `.b == "true"`       | `false`   | `true`     |
| `a: ~`         | `"~" == .a`          | `false`   | `true`     |
| `a: !!bool "yes"` | `.a == true`      | `false`   | `true`     |

Since #2785 the same class reaches mapping **keys**, with one concrete data-loss shape:
on `null: z\n~: u\n`, `to_entries | from_entries` is `{"null":"z","~":"u"}` in yq and
`{"null":"u"}` here -- both keys materialize as `Null`, stringify back to `null`, and the
second overwrites the first. `[.[] | key | tostring]` likewise prints `"null"` for the
`~` key, `keys` prints `null` where yq prints `~`, and `select(key == 1)` on a document
with both `1:` and `01:` keys matches both.

## Why it is one issue

Every row is the same missing field: the value's own text. `NumberLiteral` already
solves it for JSON-shaped numbers (`1.50`, `1e3` round-trip and compare correctly); the
fix is either widening `NumberLiteral` to any scalar spelling YAML resolves, or a
`Scalar { repr, text }` shape beside it. #1356 (`tonumber` drops `+2.0`/`007`/`.5`) is
the `tonumber` corner of the same gap.

Recorded in `docs/compliance/yq/limitations.md` (#2785's `==` and typed-key entries).

title: yq: -P/write-form path still drops one of a floated+own comment collision (#1085's DOM-path half)
body:
## Summary

#1085 fixed the "a floated anchor comment and a target node's own genuine comment can't
coexist" collision for the streaming/get-form path (`succinctly yq '.'`). The DOM path
(`-P`, and every write form: `=`, `|=`, `+=`, `del()`, ...) still shows only one of the two,
because it's a separate code path (`to_owned_with_comments` → `CommentTree`/
`NodeMeta { comment: Option<String>, .. }` in `src/jq/eval_generic.rs` and
`src/bin/succinctly/yq_runner.rs`), not the streaming cursor path in `src/yaml/light.rs`
that #1085 fixed.

```
$ printf 'a: &anc # deferred comment\n  b: # b own comment\n    c: 1\n' | yq -P '.'
a: &anc
  b: # deferred comment
  # b own comment
    c: 1
$ printf 'a: &anc # deferred comment\n  b: # b own comment\n    c: 1\n' | succinctly yq -P '.'
a: &anc
  b: # deferred comment
    c: 1
```

(Confirmed live against pinned yq v4.53.3.)

## Note: the specific single comment shown has changed since #1085

Before #1085, `-P` showed the key's own comment (`# b own comment`) and dropped the
floated one, because the parser's single `Option` slot kept whichever writer ran first
(`maybe_capture_line_comment`, the key's own capture). #1085 widened that slot to a `Vec`
and swapped the capture order (floated first, then own) so the *streaming* renderer could
emit both in the right order. The DOM path's `to_owned_with_comments` still reads only the
first entry of that `Vec` (via the existing singular `line_comment_raw()` accessor, which
now returns the *first* pushed entry) to seed `NodeMeta.comment`, so it now shows the
*floated* comment (`# deferred comment`) instead and drops the key's own — the opposite
single comment from before, not a fix. Neither shape was pinned by an existing test (the
full `yq_cli_tests.rs`/`yq_golden_tests.rs` suite passed unchanged through #1085's PR), so
this isn't a regression against any prior guarantee, just the pre-existing DOM-path gap
manifesting slightly differently now.

## Root cause / scope

`NodeMeta.comment: Option<String>` (`src/jq/eval_generic.rs`) is a single-slot structure
matching the *old* `NodeComments.line: Option<(u32,u32)>` shape #1085 moved away from at the
parser layer. Making it multi-valued (or joining both entries into one `\n`-embedded string,
mirroring how the still-unimplemented `head`/`foot` write side is meant to work per #798's
closing notes) is a distinct, separate piece of work from #1085's parser/streaming-renderer
fix:

- A different struct (`NodeMeta`, not `SemiIndex::comments`/`NodeComments`).
- A different renderer: `src/bin/succinctly/yq_runner.rs`'s DOM emitter (see
  `trailing_comment_suffix`/`append_own_comment_line`, which already implement a
  "first entry inline, rest as standalone lines at indent" split — but currently only for
  one *string* split on embedded `\n` characters coming from a `line_comment =` write, not
  for two independently-captured comments merged from the parse side).
- The seed point from the live cursor into `NodeMeta.comment` at
  `to_owned_with_comments` (`src/jq/eval_generic.rs`, ~1367-1401 and ~1445) would need to
  consume `YamlCursor::line_comments()` (the new #1085 multi-accessor) instead of the
  singular `line_comment_raw()`, and join or otherwise carry more than one comment through.

This is exactly the kind of split #798 itself went through (spinning off #2795/#2796/#2763
rather than trying to land everything in one PR) — #1085's own investigation and repro only
ever used the streaming path (`succinctly yq '.'`, no `-P` or write forms), so this DOM-path
half was out of its scope.

## Reference

- #1085 (fixed half: streaming/get-form path)
- `docs/compliance/yq/limitations.md`, "comment placement" list

title: yq: DOM route (-P/writes) prints a spurious null for an absent value it can't tell apart from an explicit one
body:
## Summary

Real yq's YAML-target printer never prints a value line for a node that had no
explicit content — an implicit-null mapping value (`a:` with nothing after the
colon), a comment-only/blank-only document, or a bare `---`/`...` marker with
nothing after it. `succinctly`'s **DOM route** (`-P`, and every write form —
`=`, `|=`, `del()`, ...) prints a spurious `null` for all of these instead,
because by the time evaluation has materialized an `OwnedValue`, "this was
genuinely absent" and "this was an explicit `null`/`~`" are indistinguishable —
`OwnedValue::Null` covers both. The plain **streaming route** (no `-P`, no
write) already gets this right for every one of these shapes.

Live-verified against pinned yq v4.53.3 and current `main` (post-#2795, PR #2841):

```
$ printf 'a:\nb: 1\n' | yq '.'                    # real yq
a:
b: 1
$ printf 'a:\nb: 1\n' | succinctly yq -P '.'       # succinctly, DOM route
a: null
b: 1
$ printf 'a:\nb: 1\n' | succinctly yq '.'          # succinctly, streaming route -- correct
a:
b: 1

$ printf 'a:\nb: 1\n' | yq -P '.a'                 # real yq: empty
$ printf 'a:\nb: 1\n' | succinctly yq -P '.a'      # succinctly: prints "null"
null

$ printf '# c\n' | yq -P '.'                       # real yq
# c
$ printf '# c\n' | succinctly yq -P '.'            # succinctly
# c
null

$ printf -- '---\n' | yq -P '.'                    # real yq
---
$ printf -- '---\n' | succinctly yq -P '.'         # succinctly
null
```

For contrast, an *explicit* null renders identically in both tools on every
route (`a: null` stays `a: null`), confirming the bug is specifically about
absence, not about `null` rendering in general:

```
$ printf 'a: null\nb: 1\n' | yq -P '.'
a: null
b: 1
$ printf 'a: null\nb: 1\n' | succinctly yq -P '.'
a: null
b: 1
```

The first repro (`a:\nb: 1\n` under `-P '.'`) is the one that matters most in
practice: an implicit-null mapping value is an extremely common YAML idiom
(a placeholder key, an optional field left blank), and this makes *every* DOM
write against a document containing one corrupt that field's rendering, not
just an edge-case document root.

## Root cause

Not new, and not specific to #2795's standalone-comment work — it just got
surfaced and precisely diagnosed while reviewing that PR. `src/yaml/parser.rs`
(current `main`, in the comment-only-document synthesis branch added by #2795's
review pass) documents it at the exact point it was re-discovered:

> Real yq's YAML-target printer suppresses the value line entirely for a
> document with no explicit content ... This was a pre-existing emitter gap,
> not new here (an explicit `---` alone with nothing after it had the
> identical `---\nnull` bug already, unrelated to comments), now closed on the
> streaming route by `YamlCursor::is_header_only_document` (`src/yaml/light.rs`)
> gating the identity path's own per-document terminator ... Still open on the
> DOM route (`-P`/a write): `OwnedValue` has no signal distinguishing this
> synthesized absence from a genuine `null`/`~` keyword or a literal `null`
> filter result once evaluation has materialized it, so the same fix can't
> safely land there without new plumbing -- tracked, not fixed, as of this
> comment.

The streaming route's fix (`YamlCursor::is_header_only_document`, gating a
per-document terminator in `light.rs`) works because it stays on the *cursor*,
which still knows whether the underlying bytes actually wrote anything. The
DOM route's `to_owned_with_comments`/`to_owned` (`src/jq/eval_generic.rs`)
converts straight to `OwnedValue::Null` with no such signal carried forward,
and `emit_yaml_value`/`emit_yaml_value_at_depth`
(`src/bin/succinctly/yq_runner.rs`) has no way to tell it apart from a real
null once it gets there.

## Scope

Fixing this for real needs the DOM pipeline to carry an "explicit vs. absent"
bit alongside a null value from cursor through to the emitter — plausibly on
`CommentTree`/`NodeMeta` (already a shape-parallel side channel the DOM path
threads through `reconcile_presentation_at_depth`/`strip_presentation_style_at_depth`
for comments/style/anchor) rather than widening `OwnedValue` itself, which is
shared with the JSON evaluator and has no such concept there (JSON has no
"implicit null" — `#747`/`#1132`'s stated reasons for keeping `OwnedValue`
metadata-free). Both `emit_yaml_value_at_depth`'s object-field arm (the
`key_comment_if_value_absent`/`defers_to_own_block` branches already
distinguish some absent-value shapes for comment-placement purposes) and the
root wrapper in `output_value` would need to consult it.

Four confirmed repro shapes, all on the DOM route only:
- a mapping field with a deferred/implicit-null value (`a:` then a sibling key)
- a document that is comment-only or blank-only
- an explicit `---`/`...` marker with nothing following it
- (likely, untested here) the same shapes nested deeper, or as an array element

## Reference

- #2795 (PR #2841) — where this was found and precisely diagnosed, but
  explicitly left open as out of that PR's scope
- `src/yaml/parser.rs`'s comment-only-document synthesis branch (current
  `main`) — the exact code-level tracking note quoted above
- `src/yaml/light.rs`'s `YamlCursor::is_header_only_document` — the streaming
  route's already-working fix, useful as a reference for what signal the DOM
  route is missing

title: yq: JSON flow-mapping token-pairing grammar (#2777) needs route unification for --inplace/--slurp/--eval-all
body:
## Context

#2777 (fixed in this issue's own PR) adds real yq's token-pairing grammar for
JSON-sourced flow mappings (`-p json`'s `{...}`) on the "plain" route
(`YamlIndex`-backed parsing, used by ordinary evaluation without
`--inplace`/`--slurp`/`--eval-all`). Two things were deliberately scoped out
of that fix, both documented in `docs/compliance/yq/limitations.md`'s
"Closed by #2777" section:

## 1. Route unification (DOM bridge still uses the old strict grammar)

`--inplace`/`--slurp`/`--eval-all` materialize JSON input through a separate
code path — `yq_runner::parse_input`'s `InputFormat::Json` arm, which uses
`JsonIndex` + `to_owned_canonicalizing_numbers_at_depth` rather than
`YamlIndex::build_json_sourced`. That route still applies #1975's own
stricter-than-real-yq JSON grammar, so it does not get #2777's leniency:

```console
$ printf '{"a":1 "b":2}' > /tmp/f.json
$ yq -p json -o json -I0 --inplace '.' /tmp/f.json && cat /tmp/f.json
{"a":1,"b":2}
$ succinctly yq -p json -o json -I0 --inplace '.' /tmp/f.json
Error: Invalid JSON text: expected ',' or '}', found '"'
```

Fixing this means making `yq_runner::parse_input`'s `InputFormat::Json` arm
build through `YamlIndex::build_json_sourced` too (instead of `JsonIndex`),
which would also require carrying `JsonIndex`'s own number-canonicalization
pass over to the YAML-cursor-backed walk. This is a separate, larger change
that touches the destructive `--inplace` write path, so it needs its own
careful test coverage (proving nothing is written on a rejected file, and
that `--inplace` now rewrites what real yq rewrites) rather than being
folded into #2777's own fix.

## 2. "Any bracket ends the loop" is not reproduced

Real yq's token scanner treats *every* bracket character (`{`, `}`, `[`,
`]`) as a `Delim` that ends the *current* object's key-reading loop the
instant one is seen — not just its own matching closing brace:

```console
$ printf '{"a":1 ]}' | yq -p json -o json -I0 '.'
{"a":1}
$ printf '{[1]:2}' | yq -p json -o json -I0 '.'
{}
```

Whatever is left unconsumed in that case is then read as the *next*
top-level document by yq's own stream evaluator, whose own trailing-content
handling is itself inconsistent (some leftover shapes produce no visible
error at all; others print a stream-decode error to stderr while still
emitting the correct value and exiting 0). Reproducing this faithfully would
mean modelling a second, top-level-only decoder loop with the same
inconsistency, for a shape (a bare bracket standing in for a key, with no
quotes at all) that essentially never occurs in real-world JSON.

succinctly currently reports an ordinary parse error for a `{`/`[`/`]` found
where a key is expected (always failing the whole document cleanly), rather
than silently producing a truncated one — a safe-direction divergence, never
a wrong value, just a narrower acceptance set than the reference's own
accidental leniency here.

## Suggested approach

- For (1): thread `YamlIndex::build_json_sourced` through
  `yq_runner::parse_input`'s JSON arm, replacing `JsonIndex`; verify
  `parse_input_m2_parity`'s depth pre-check still holds (the YAML parser
  already enforces `MAX_NESTING_DEPTH` at parse time).
- For (2): lower priority given how rarely a bare bracket appears where a
  key is expected in real-world JSON; if tackled, needs its own model of
  yq's inconsistent trailing-content handling, which may be more trouble
  than it's worth to chase byte-for-byte.

Related: #2777, #1975, #2279, #2778, #2781, #2845.

title: perf(jq): a fold under an `as` binding (#2889 embed table active) skips the owned step and stays O(n²)
body:
## Summary

Follow-up from #3138. `fold_step_each` (`src/jq/eval.rs`) skips `try_eval_owned_step` entirely while `embed_table_active()` (#2889). So a fold running inside an `as` binding that holds a document node still takes the reindex bridge on every step and stays O(n²):

```bash
succinctly jq '. as $d | reduce $d.users[0:4000][] as $r ({}; .[$r.name] = $r.score) | length' users.json
```

On Apple M5 Max (`json generate 2mb -p users`), N=4,000 takes 3.44 s both before and after #3138. Without the `. as $d` wrapper, the same fold is at the ~40 ms process floor after #3138.

## Why it is skipped

The embed table lets a value that *is* a bound node's own value be answered as that node, not as a re-indexed copy (#2889). The owned step never reaches a resolver, so it may be safe to run while the table is active. Nobody has checked that yet, which is why #3138 left this branch unchanged.

## What would fix it

Show that `owned_assign_step` (and the #2157 arithmetic arm) can run while the embed table is active without changing any `path()`, `$__loc__` or marker output. #3181 is the known interaction between markers and the fold UPDATE. Then lift the `embed_table_active()` guard for those shapes. `owned_assign_step_fold_rows_match_jq_3138` already pins the output of this case.

title: jq: path register not kept across a navigating recursion's first output (`$x` after `..`/`recurse(f)` on an untracked input)
body:
**Severity: Low.** succinctly refuses where jq answers, in `path()`/`del()`/assignment. It is always a loud error, never a silent wrong write.

## Summary

In jq, recursion on an untracked input produces its first output (the input itself) without moving the path register. A later `$x` bound earlier in the pipeline still matches the register and gets a path back. Only the *next* step of the recursion, which does navigate, raises the path error. succinctly doesn't keep the register across that first output: the whole recursion stage loses it, so `$x` is refused "with result …" before jq's own error point is reached.

Found while fixing #2764 (branch `issue-2764-untracked-path-eager-refusal`, `fb7fc21d5`). That work fixed the case where `f` does not navigate (`recurse(empty)`, `recurse(.+1; .<3)`: `cannot_move_register` now admits them). This issue covers the recursions whose `f` *does* navigate, including bare `..`/`recurse` from #2761.

All confirmed live against jq 1.7.1:

```console
$ echo '{"a":{"b":{"b":null}},"c":2}' | jq -c 'path(. as $x | 1 | .. | $x)'
[]
jq: error (at <stdin>:1): Invalid path expression near attempt to iterate through 1
$ ... | succinctly jq -c 'path(. as $x | 1 | .. | $x)'
jq: error (at <stdin>:1): Invalid path expression with result {"a":{"b":{"b":null}},"c":2}

$ ... | jq -c 'path(.a as $y | .a | 5 | .. | $y)'          # same for bare `recurse`
["a"]
jq: error (at <stdin>:1): Invalid path expression near attempt to iterate through 5
$ ... | succinctly jq -c 'path(.a as $y | .a | 5 | .. | $y)'
jq: error (at <stdin>:1): Invalid path expression with result {"b":{"b":null}}

$ ... | jq -c 'path(. as $x | 1 | recurse(.[]?) | $x)'
[]
jq: error (at <stdin>:1): Invalid path expression near attempt to iterate through 1
$ ... | succinctly jq -c 'path(. as $x | 1 | recurse(.[]?) | $x)'
jq: error (at <stdin>:1): Invalid path expression with result {"a":{"b":{"b":null}},"c":2}

$ ... | jq -c 'path(. as $x | 1 | try recurse(.a) | $x)'   # refuse where jq accepts
[]
$ ... | succinctly jq -c 'path(. as $x | 1 | try recurse(.a) | $x)'
jq: error (at <stdin>:1): Invalid path expression with result {"a":{"b":{"b":null}},"c":2}
```

## Where

`resolve_seq_stage` decides once per stage whether the register survives (`stage_preserves_register`, from `cannot_move_register(element)`). The recurse family's answer depends on the *branch*, not the expression: the first output (`recurse_family_root_seed`, a passthrough with zero path components) keeps the register, and every later output comes from navigating. `getpath` has the same per-branch shape and is handled by `getpath_preserves_register` (#2896). A similar per-branch check for the recurse family's first output (zero components, jq mode, untracked input) is the likely fix. Then check that the later navigation error still comes out with jq's "near attempt" wording and can still be caught by `try`.

## Verification

Before trusting any `del`/`=` result, run the rows above together with their `del(... | $x | .c)` / `(... | $x | .c) |= 9` forms and compare against jq, including under `try`. Widening what gets accepted can hide silent write discards (#3267).

title: perf(jq): a pipe-shaped def chain and a filter naming many defs are still quadratic in the number of top-level defs (#3307 follow-up)
body:
**Severity: Low**

## Summary

After #3307 (#3452) a program of many top-level defs installs in linear time and memory, but two other passes still cost quadratic time in the number of defs.

## Repro

`succinctly jq -n -f prog.jq`, release build of `main` after #3452, Apple M-series (laptop, indicative; the growth per doubling is the point).

| shape                                                       | defs M | time      |
|-------------------------------------------------------------|-------:|-----------|
| `def f0: 0; def f1: f0 \| . + 1; ...; f{M-1}` (pipe chain) | 3000   | 0.15 s    |
|                                                             | 6000   | 0.44 s    |
|                                                             | 12000  | 2.16 s    |
| the same chain written `f{i-1} + 1`                        | 12000  | ~0.1 s (linear) |
| `def g0: 0; ...; [g0, g1, ..., g{M-1}] \| length`          | 24000  | ~1.1 s (measured in the #3452 review) |

## Root cause

1. **Pipe chain:** `needs_path_context` (`src/jq/eval.rs`) recurses through every `DefCall` body (`needs_path_context(&def.body) || args.iter().any(...)`) and its `FuncDef` arm, unmemoised, and is re-run per pipe evaluation from `eval_each_pipe_generic` (`src/jq/eval_generic.rs`). A pipe-shaped dependency chain therefore walks the whole chain on every evaluation of every level. A `sample` at M=20000 put nearly every eval-thread sample there. The `+` spelling never asks, so it stays linear. Related, pre-existing: the `needs_path_context` superlinearity on recursive defs (#2626).
2. **Resolver scan:** `resolve::reach_in_scope`/`scan_scope` (and `ModuleRun::parse` per scope entry) resolve each call by a linear reverse scan of every def in scope, so a filter that names `M` defs is `O(M x calls)` before evaluation starts. The evaluator's own installer (`SpineInstaller` in `src/jq/eval.rs`) is name-indexed since #3307; the resolver and the yq write-shape analysis (`DefScope::resolve`) are two more scope structures with different complexity.

## Why this is separate from #3307

#3307 is the install (`bind_def` rebuilding and retaining the program below every def). These are different passes with different fixes, and each was already present, and much worse, before it.

## Suggested fix direction

Memoise `needs_path_context` per def body (a `SharedArg`-style `Cell` on `FuncDefData`, or compute once when the def is frozen); index the resolver's scope by name so a lookup is `O(log M)`. Both are checkable by the same `def f_i` chain at 3000/6000/12000 defs, doubling.

title: jq: foreach source that navigates then runs an opaque builtin (`first`, `add`, def) loses the register -- wrong path/write on null documents
body:
## Summary

Residual of #2159. A `foreach` source that navigates and then runs a stage the path resolver cannot see inside (`first`, `add`, a user `def` -- anything `!stage_preserves_register`) leaves jq's path register at a position the resolver cannot know: jq indexes *within* the builtin (`first` is `.[0]`, so `.a|first` moves the register to `["a",0]`). #2159's fix models such an element as `MovedRegister::Lost`: the per-step register is untracked, so UPDATE/EXTRACT navigation refuses. That never fabricates a path, but it is not jq's answer either.

## Repro (jq 1.7.1 vs `succinctly jq`, both `path()` and the write form)

```console
$ echo null | jq -c 'path(foreach (.a|first) as $k (.; .))'
["a",0]
$ echo null | succinctly jq -c 'path(foreach (.a|first) as $k (.; .))'
[]

$ echo null | jq -c '(foreach (.a|first) as $k (.; .)) = 9'
{"a":[9]}
$ echo null | succinctly jq -c '(foreach (.a|first) as $k (.; .)) = 9'
9                                     # wrong write, exit 0

$ echo '{"a":null,"b":null}' | jq -c 'path(foreach (.a|first) as $k (null; .))'
["a",0]
$ echo '{"a":null,"b":null}' | succinctly jq -c 'path(foreach (.a|first) as $k (null; .))'
# error (exit 5) -- REJECT
```

The first two are **both-ok-differ** and the second is a wrong *write* on a `null` document (the accumulator `null` is kind-identical to the lost register, so the terminal check accepts it at the wrong position). They are unchanged from before #2159's fix, not a regression of it.

## Measured

`.ai/scratch/sweep-2159.py` (61,824 cases, `path(...)` and `(...) = 9`, 7 inputs) after #2159's fix: every residual (100 both-ok-differ, ~245 REJECT, 6 both-error-differ) is a `first` / `add?` source or one of the two identity quirks in the sibling issue. `FABRICATE` is 0.

## Direction

Either (a) model the builtins that index internally (`first` = `.[0]`, `last` = `.[-1]`, `add`, `min_by`...) as navigation in `resolve_seq` so they never reach `Lost`, or (b) make the `Lost` arm poison the terminal `path()` check too (an emission after a lost register must refuse rather than compare against the persistent one). (b) removes the wrong-write; (a) also recovers the REJECTs.

title: jq: foreach per-step register does not carry accumulator identity across source elements, nor `tostring` of a string
body:
## Summary

Two pointer-identity divergences left in `foreach`'s per-step register after #2159. Both are *refusals* (jq answers, succinctly errors); neither can fabricate a path. Both exist on `main` before #2159 (verified with an unfixed binary), so they are not regressions.

### 1. The accumulator's identity is not carried from one source element to the next

```console
$ echo '{"a":{"a":1},"b":{"c":2}}' | jq -c 'path(foreach (1, .a) as $k (.; .a))'
["a"]
["a","a"]
$ echo '{"a":{"a":1},"b":{"c":2}}' | succinctly jq -c 'path(foreach (1, .a) as $k (.; .a))'
["a"]
jq: error ... Invalid path expression near attempt to access element "a" of {"a":1}
```

Step 1's UPDATE (`.a`) leaves the accumulator pointing at `{"a":1}` -- the very node element 2's `.a` then moves the register onto, so jq's `jv_identical` holds and the second UPDATE navigates. `resolve_foreach` seeds each step's `at_register` from `register_identical(register, state, state_snapshot)`, and `state_snapshot` (the previous step's provenance) does not certify against the new step's frame.

### 2. `tostring` of a string is the same `jv`

```console
$ echo '{"a":[1,2],"b":"s"}' | jq -c 'path(foreach (.b|tostring) as $k (.; $k))'
["b"]
$ echo '{"a":[1,2],"b":"s"}' | succinctly jq -c 'path(foreach (.b|tostring) as $k (.; $k))'
# error
```

`tostring` returns its input unchanged for a string, so `$k` is pointer-identical to the register at `.b`. `OwnedValue` has no node identity; this is one more instance of what #3191 (thin refcounted string for scalar node identity) would address.

## Measured

`.ai/scratch/sweep-2159.py`: 7 rows after #2159's fix, all in `.b|tostring` (6) and `1, (.a|tostring)` (1).

title: jq: move yq's DOM route onto the converged eval() once the generic bridge is cheap for tiny values (#3457 follow-up)
body:
**Severity: Low** (performance and a second evaluator kept alive; no wrong answers)

## Summary

#3457 made the library `succinctly::jq::eval` the CLI's evaluator. `succinctly yq`'s DOM route (`-R` lines, `--inplace`, `--slurp`, writes, `--arg`) was left on the previous evaluator through the hidden `jq::eval_reindexed` (the hybrid `eval` used to be: generic evaluator for a query that reads path context, `eval_full` otherwise), because moving it cost speed.

Measured on an M4 Pro (interleaved `scripts/ab-cli.py`, 9 reps, the `users` document as 1 MB and 10 MB of `-R` lines, output identical):

| query                    | +wall through the converged `eval` |
|--------------------------|------------------------------------|
| `select(test("age"))`    | +21% (1 MB), +37% (10 MB)          |
| `. + "x"`                | +4% to +9%                         |
| `.`, `length`            | within the ±1% noise floor         |

Cause (from a `sample` profile): the generic evaluator answers a builtin it has no native arm for (`test`, `+`, ...) through `bridge_to_full_evaluator`, which serializes the value and builds a `JsonIndex` again on every call. `-R` makes one call per line, on tiny documents, so that fixed cost dominates.

## Why it matters

- Two evaluators stay reachable from the CLI (yq's DOM route on `eval.rs`, everything else on the generic one), and `eval_reindexed` is a second router (`needs_path_context`) that can drift from `eval`.
- Cursor-metadata builtins differ by route on that path: `.c | line` is `1` through `eval`, and the fixed default `0` through `eval_reindexed`.

## Direction

Make the bridge cheap for a small owned value (skip the re-index when the value is already a decoded `OwnedValue`, or add native generic arms for the hot builtins), then move yq's two call sites in `yq_runner.rs` onto `eval` and delete `eval_reindexed`. Gate on the same `-R` A/B: no row outside the control's noise floor.

## Related

#3457 (the convergence and the measurements), #3427, #3429.

title: jq: path-mode `foreach` evaluates its UPDATE before a consumer can stop it
body:
**Severity: Low** (a side effect runs for outputs the consumer never asked for)

Found while working on #3293 slice 5. Reproduced on `main` @ `54529af84`, against `/usr/bin/jq` 1.7.1. No `?//` is involved.

Path-mode `foreach` evaluates its UPDATE to completion before its consumer can stop it. Value-mode `foreach` (#2668, `fold_step_each`) and path-mode `reduce` are lazy enough to match jq here; path-mode `foreach` UPDATE is the one left:

```console
$ echo '{"a":{"a":1}}' | jq -c '[first(path(foreach 1 as $x (.; .[("a"|stderr), ("b"|stderr)]))), 9]'
a[["a"],9]
$ echo '{"a":{"a":1}}' | succinctly jq -c '[first(path(foreach 1 as $x (.; .[("a"|stderr), ("b"|stderr)]))), 9]'
ab[["a"],9]
$ echo '{"a":{"a":1}}' | succinctly jq -c '[first(foreach 1 as $x (.; .[("a"|stderr), ("b"|stderr)])), 9]'    # value mode
a[{"a":1},9]
```

The `?//` consequence, which is how #3293 slice 5 found it: a `?//` inside the UPDATE never sees the consumer's stop, so it is never asked to retry, and a retry that jq raises is missed:

```console
$ F='[first(path(foreach 1 as $x (.; .[([["a"]] as [$q] ?// $b | ("A"|stderr) | if $q then "a" else error("E2") end)]))), 9]'
$ echo '{"a":{"a":1}}' | jq -c "$F"
AAjq: error (at <stdin>:1): E2
$ echo '{"a":{"a":1}}' | succinctly jq -c "$F"
A[["a"],9]
```

This is the #2180/#2668 "materialized before the consumer" family, not a stale-stash slot: no `?//` retry happens at all, so no `StashedVerdict` can supersede anything. `scripts/jq-alt-retry-oracle-sweep.sh` lists the `ix-foreach` rows that hit it as known against this issue.

title: jq: an array collector over an owned-input `key` chain prints `[]` after the error it raises
body:
Found while working #3293 slice 9 (pre-existing, no `?//` involved).

```
$ succinctly jq -nc '{"a":1} | [(error("E2")) | key]'
jq: error (at <unknown>): E2
[]
$ echo '{"a":1}' | succinctly jq -c '[(error("E2")) | key]'      # cursor route
jq: error (at <stdin>:1): E2
$ echo '{"a":1}' | jq -c '[path(error("E2"))]'                  # jq 1.7.1
jq: error (at <stdin>:1): E2
```

`[(.a, error("E2")) | key]` over an owned input prints `["a"]` after the error, where the cursor route prints nothing. jq's `[...]` never emits the partial array once its body raises. The owned-identity walk's "deliver the prefix, then the escape" rule (#2495) reaches the array collector. `key` is succinctly's; the oracle is `[path(...)]`.

Not a stale-slot bug, so it stays out of #3293. #3293 slice 9's owned-route run of the `RETRY_ROWS_PATH_CONTEXT_COND_3293` table skips its one row that hits this.

title: jq: `skip(n; f) | key` over an owned input names the input's key, not the skipped-to element's
body:
Found while working #3293 slice 9 (pre-existing, no `?//` involved).

```
$ succinctly jq -nc '{"a":{"b":[1,2]}} | .a | skip(1; .b[]) | key'
"a"
$ echo '{"a":{"b":[1,2]}}' | succinctly jq -c '.a | skip(1; .b[]) | key'    # cursor route
1
```

jq 1.7.1 has no `skip`; by `limit`'s model (`path(.a | limit(1; .b[]))` is `["a","b",0]`) the answer is the element's own index, as the cursor route gives. The owned route answers the position of the `skip` stage's input instead. Not a stale-slot bug, so it stays out of #3293.

title: jq: `limit(n; .[] | <retrying body>) | key` runs the retry past `limit`'s stop on the cursor route
body:
Found while working #3293 slice 9 (cursor route; the owned route matches jq).

```
$ echo '{"a":[1,2]}' | succinctly jq -c '.a | limit(1; .[] | if ([1] as $q ?// $b | ("A"|stderr) as $_ | $q) then error("E") else . end) | key'
AAAA0
$ echo '{"a":[1,2]}' | jq -c 'path(.a | limit(1; .[] | if ([1] as $q ?// $b | ("A"|stderr) as $_ | $q) then error("E") else . end)) | last'
AA0
```

The value-mode spelling (no `key`) is `AA1` on both. Without a `?//` in the body, `limit(1; .[] | ("A"|stderr) as $_ | .) | key` prints a single `A`, so the extra attempts come from a `?//` retrying past `limit`'s own stop in the path-context walk's `limit` arm (`path_context_step_generic`, #3293 slice 7). Probably the same #2180/#3470 "materialized before the consumer" family; re-check when picking it up.
